formality: Formal, polite register (합니다/습니다체) throughout — the standard register for professional Korean B2B/security software, not casual speech. Korean UI conventionally omits the subject/pronoun ('you'), so there is no need for 당신/귀하 anywhere in the copy.
styleNotes: System messages, confirmations and errors use the formal -습니다/-합니다 ending, never a casual speech level. Buttons and menu labels stay in noun-phrase form (저장, 적용, 삭제) rather than imperative verb endings (저장하세요). Keep transliterations that are already standard among Korean hashcat/security practitioners (해시, 에이전트, 워크플로우, 벤치마크, 마스크) instead of coining unfamiliar pure-Korean terms, but don't over-apply this to generic words that translate naturally (해시 목록, not a forced loanword). Write noun compounds with a space between independent words (해시 목록, 공격 모드) for readability, and leave every term in terms.json's doNotTranslate list (algorithm/protocol names, acronyms, units like GH/s) untouched.

hash.note: standard Korean security term for password hash values

hash type.note: fixed from the draft's '해시 종류': '유형' matches how Korean form/dropdown labels name a type selector (파일 유형, 회원 유형); '종류' reads more like a casual list of kinds than a field label

crack.note: verb; widely used in Korean security community

cracked.note: past participle adjective, passive of 크래킹하다

potfile.note: hashcat-specific technical term, kept as is

client potfile.note: potfile kept English per the glossary, with the Korean noun modifier '클라이언트' prepended

wordlist.note: standard transliteration in Korean security tools

mask.note: standard transliteration in hashcat Korean documentation

brute force.note: common transliteration in the Korean hashcat community; alternative: 무차별 대입 (more literal, more formal register)

association attack.note: fixed from the draft's '어소시에이션 공격': that transliteration is opaque since hashcat's mode 9 has no established Korean name yet; '연관' already means 'association' in Korean CS usage (연관 규칙 = association rule), so '연관 공격' is understandable without first knowing hashcat's English mode name

keyspace.note: standard transliteration in Korean hashcat documentation

task.note: fixed from the draft's '작업' (identical to 'job'): a job contains many tasks, so giving both the same Korean word hides that hierarchy in the UI (job lists and task/chunk assignments would read identically); '태스크' is the transliteration Korean docs for Jenkins/Kubernetes/Spark already use for the sub-unit of a job

job.note: kept distinct from 'task' (태스크, see above) so the two scheduling levels are not ambiguous in the UI

max agents.note: added '수' (count): '최대 에이전트' alone reads as a single agent labeled 'maximum', not a limit on how many agents a job may use

overflow.note: fixed from the draft's '오버플로우': that loanword is strongly associated with buffer-overflow vulnerabilities in Korean security usage, a confusing association for a scheduling/allocation setting; '초과' (beyond the limit/excess) says what it means without the clash

hash rate.note: fixed from the draft's '해시율': '해시레이트' is the term Korean hashcat and GPU-mining communities actually use (same GPUs, shared vocabulary); '해시율' is a rare calque few readers will recognize at a glance

agent.note: standard transliteration in system agent terminology

claim code.note: fixed from the draft's '클레임 코드': in everyday Korean business usage '클레임' means a customer complaint (클레임을 걸다 = to file a complaint), not 'to claim/take'; '등록 코드' (registration code) says what the code is actually used for

offline buffer.note: fixed '유예 시간' to '유예 기간': '유예기간' (grace period) is the standard Korean collocation (cf. 납부 유예기간); '유예 시간' is less idiomatic

binary.note: standard transliteration; refers to the executable hashcat binary

client.note: customer/engagement in business context; '클라이언트' already carries this business-customer sense in Korean consulting/agency usage (클라이언트사, 클라이언트 미팅), not only the software client-server sense

member.note: common in modern Korean SaaS UI; alternative: 구성원 (more formal)

archive.note: verb/noun for hiding data without deleting; matches the Korean 'Archive' convention used by Gmail etc.

apply.note: button action verb, used in noun form per style notes

SAN.note: Subject Alternative Name; technical certificate field, kept as the acronym

cloud fleet.note: '플릿' matches AWS's own Korean localization for fleets of cloud instances

provisioning.note: standard transliteration for automated instance launch

drain.note: in scheduling context: allow work to finish without starting new work; matches Kubernetes 'node drain' Korean usage

teardown.note: destroying a cloud instance; matches AWS's own Korean term for instance termination (인스턴스 종료)

two-factor authentication.note: MFA; kept over the more colloquial '2단계 인증' (two-step verification) because that phrase technically describes a different, looser guarantee than genuine two-factor authentication
